{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"1e034a0e824199f4c5fb535799f7443f8cc0d2633cb6fd941606690b0b858ad2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Turns and intersections: signals, turning lanes, U-turns, right of way and roundabouts","heading":"C2 — Turn and intersection confusables: red-light turns by road type, city versus rural U-turn distances, four-way versus two-way stops, and roundabout entry versus exit","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Turn and intersection confusables: red-light turns by road type, city versus rural U-turn distances, four-way versus two-way stops, and roundabout entry versus exit
Confusable pairs from the turns and intersections pages, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
Signal lights work at any time, but hand-and-arm signals are limited to daylight with a clear view of 1,000 feet, so darkness or poor visibility means lights only. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable hand signals versus signal lights; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
The 100-foot signal rule applies when you are already moving in traffic, while leaving a curb you signal long enough to warn traffic rather than for a set distance. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable moving signal versus curb signal; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A02
Crossing a bike lane during a turn is allowed, but merging into the bike lane ahead of the turn is not. [A02]
Why it matters: group turning and bicycles; confusable crossing versus entering a bike lane; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A02
A right turn starts as close as possible to the right curb or road edge, while a left turn on a two-way road starts in the lane just right of the center line. [A02]
Why it matters: group turn position; confusable right-turn start versus left-turn start; difficulty easy.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A02
Before a right turn and before a left turn the same head check applies: left, ahead, right, then left again. [A02]
Why it matters: group turn scanning; confusable scan order for right versus left turns; difficulty easy.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A03
A left turn from one one-way road onto another is allowed on red after a stop and yield, but a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road is never allowed on red. [A03]
Why it matters: group red-light turns; confusable one-way target versus two-way target; difficulty hard.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A03
Turning from a two-way road onto a one-way road may be made against a red light after stopping and yielding, the opposite of a left turn onto a two-way road on red. [A03]
Why it matters: group red-light turns; confusable two-way to one-way versus left onto two-way; difficulty hard.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A03
Leaving a one-way road to turn left, you start from the lane nearest the left curb whether the new road is one-way or two-way; only the lane you end in changes. [A03]
Why it matters: group turn lanes; confusable start lane versus end lane; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A04
The U-turn visibility distance is 500 feet inside city limits but 1,000 feet outside city limits. [A04]
Why it matters: group U-turns; confusable city distance versus rural distance; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A04
A U-turn at a signal-controlled intersection is banned unless a sign allows it, whereas a U-turn between intersections in a city is banned outright. [A04]
Why it matters: group U-turns; confusable signal intersection versus mid-block; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A05
At a four-way stop the first driver to stop goes first by courtesy, while at a two-way stop with facing signs the driver turning left yields to oncoming straight traffic. [A05]
Why it matters: group stop-sign right of way; confusable four-way versus two-way stop; difficulty hard.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A05
At an uncontrolled intersection you yield to vehicles already in it or coming from the right, while at an uncontrolled T intersection the driver on the ending road yields to through traffic. [A05]
Why it matters: group uncontrolled intersections; confusable crossroads versus T intersection; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A05
A green light lets you go only if there is space for your vehicle beyond the intersection; a green light does not mean the way through is clear. [A05]
Why it matters: group signals at intersections; confusable green light versus room to clear; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A06
Entering a roundabout you yield to circulating and exiting traffic, while leaving it you give a right turn signal and watch the crosswalk. [A06]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; confusable entry duty versus exit duty; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A06
A bicyclist approaching a roundabout may either merge with traffic or use the sidewalk, and one who merges gets the full travel lane with no passing inside. [A06]
Why it matters: group roundabouts and bicycles; confusable merging rider versus sidewalk rider; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A07
For an emergency vehicle outside a roundabout you stay out and pull right, but once inside you keep moving, exit and then pull over; stopping in the circle is never correct. [A07]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; confusable before entering versus already inside; difficulty hard.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A07
In a multi-lane roundabout you choose the lane for your exit before entering and hold it, rather than changing lanes once inside. [A07]
Why it matters: group multi-lane roundabouts; confusable lane choice before entry versus lane change inside; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0052]
